pairs.question: Si quis fundum, quem putabat se possidere, defenderit, mox emerit: re secundum petitorem iudicata an restituere cogatur?
pairs.answer: Si actori iterum petenti obiciatur exceptio rei iudicatae, replicare eum oportere de re secundum se iudicata.
pairs.derivation: Direct interrogative ending in '?' in the source. Answer span starts after dropping the speech-tag framing 'et ait neratius,' and takes Neratius's operative reply to its full stop; nothing follows in this section. Section marker 'Dig. 44.2.9.1' and jurist-citation line 'Ulpianus 75 ad ed.' stripped as scaffolding.

pairs.question: Si in arbitrum compromiserimus, deinde cum non stetissem ob adversam valitudinem, poena commissa est, an uti possim doli exceptione?
pairs.derivation: Direct interrogative ending in '?'. Answer is Pomponius's reply with the speech tag 'et ait pomponius' dropped and the first word capitalized; the reply is a single sentence answering the question. Section marker and 'Ulpianus 76 ad ed.' citation stripped.

pairs.question: Si quis ex uncia heres sit scriptus, ex qua ducenta consequi potuit, deinde propter hoc legatum, in quo centum erant, praetulit, ne molestiis hereditariis implicaretur: an, si legatum petat, exceptione doli mali summoveatur?
pairs.derivation: Direct interrogative ending in '?'. Answer is Julian's response with speech tag 'et ait iulianus' dropped and first word capitalized. Cut stops at the first full stop; the subsequent 'quod si a substituto pretium accepit...' introduces a different sub-case (the heir who took a price not to enter) and is not the answer to this question. Section marker and citation line stripped.

pairs.question: Fideiussor evictionis nomine condemnatus id praedium, quod evictum est, et omnia praestare paratus est, quae iure empti continentur: quaero, an agentem emptorem exceptione ex causa iudicati doli mali summovere potest?
pairs.answer: Exceptionem quidem opponi posse, iudicem autem aestimaturum, ut pro damnis emptori satisfiat.
pairs.derivation: Consultation question (Scaevola, responsa): the case is set up and then 'quaero, an ... summovere potest' poses the question; terminal full stop normalized to '?'. Answer takes the responsum with the speech tag 'respondit' dropped; it is a single sentence directly answering. Section marker 'Dig. 44.4.15' and citation 'Hermogenianus 6 iuris epit.'/'Scaevola 5 resp.' line stripped.

pairs.question: Lucio titio cum ex causa iudicati pecunia deberetur et eidem debitori aliam pecuniam crederet, in cautione pecuniae creditae non adiecit sibi praeter eam pecuniam debitam sibi ex causa iudicati: quaero, an integrae sint utraeque lucio titio petitiones?
pairs.answer: Nihil proponi, cur non sint integrae.
pairs.derivation: Consultation question (Paulus, responsa): case set up, then 'quaero, an integrae sint utraeque lucio titio petitiones'; terminal full stop normalized to '?'. Answer is the responsum with the speech tag 'paulus respondit' dropped. Section marker 'Dig. 44.7.29' and citation 'Paulus 4 resp.' line stripped.
